one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: September revenue on Oct 8, 2026 (13:30 Taiwan time, per TSMC calendar; corrected from ~Oct 9), Q3 results and Q4 guidance on Oct 15 (quiet period Oct 5-14) [17], and the FOMC on Oct 27-28 after a Sep 16 hike, with the 10y at ~5.29% [24,25]. July+August revenue was NT$982B [2], so September only has to match August for a beat; UBS expects ~$45.7B revenue and 67.1% GM [8]. The beat is expected. The swing factors are Q4 GM (N2 dilution of 3-4pt [18]) and early 2027 capex color, which UBS now puts at $90B. In July a record quarter still saw the ADR fall ~4% [3]. Rising long yields are a modest headwind for the multiple within the month. I keep the median a touch above spot (~$462) with a log-sd of ~12%, slightly above the 11.4% normal monthly vol to reflect earnings. That is near-symmetric with no strong directional call.

fair_value.method: 70% P/E: Oct-2027 NTM EPS $23.90 less a 3% haircut = $23.18 x 18.5x = $429. 30% FCF yield: NTM FCF ~$11.2/ADR ($90B FY27 and $105B FY28 capex, 63.5% OCF margin) at 2.85% = $393. Blended fair value ~$418, ~9% below spot.

FY27 consensus net income (~$114B = 49.5% of revenue [4]) plus D&A of ~14% of revenue (Q2 run-rate NT$198.5B/qtr [23], rising with capex) is ~63.5% before working capital and supplier prepayments. bear.story: A 2027 AI digestion: hyperscaler D&A catches up and capex growth slows sharply [7,20], Nvidia (>20% of revenue [14]) trims orders, and N2/overseas dilution plus equipment inflation take GM toward ~60% [26]. FY28 EPS stalls near ~$21 and the multiple de-rates to ~14x with 5%+ long rates [24]. A non-invasion Taiwan or Section 232 shock [11] would also land here.

base.story: Consensus EPS growth (~30% in FY27 [4]) is delivered, helped by largely-priced 2027 wafer price increases, but the multiple compresses from ~21x to ~20x NTM ($23.9) as growth decelerates, capex rises to ~$90B and long rates stay above 5%. The stock is modestly up.

bull.story: AI demand keeps surprising (UBS-style +40% 2027 revenue to ~$240B at ~67% GM [8]), FY28 EPS reaches ~$27, and the stock holds ~24x on N2/A16 monopoly pricing despite high rates.

thesis_break_reason: $330 is ~28% below spot, ~15x the confirmed $21.93 FY27 consensus, and near the March 2026 low. A move there would most likely mean the 2027 earnings path is being cut (an AI order pause, Nvidia or hyperscaler capex cuts, or a structural GM reset below ~58%) or that a geopolitical or tariff discount is being priced in, not ordinary 40%-vol multiple noise. Unchanged from round 1, and it matches the supervisor's level.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's evidence led me to make three corrections. (1) The VIS gain (NT$63.2B, confirmed in the 2Q26 management report [23]) is a 2026 one-off not in FY27/28 consensus, so my 5% EPS haircut double-counted. I cut it to 3%, keeping the N2/overseas GM dilution, equipment-inflation and depreciation-wall components [7,8,18,26]. (2) I checked the OCF margin against primary data. H1 2026 OCF/revenue was 61.7%, but Q2 carried the annual NT$188B tax payment and a working-capital build [23]; consensus net income plus rising D&A gives ~63.5%. I also rolled the FCF leg to NTM at Oct-2027 using UBS's $105B 2028 capex. (3) I verified the 10y at ~5.29% on Sep 30 (highest since 2007) [24,25]. That cuts both ways for me: it supports a below-group multiple, so I move only to 18.5x rather than the supervisor's 19.5x, and it raises my FCF yield to 2.85%. The UBS $90B/$240.7B figures are still only reachable through a Substack recap [8], and a re-search surfaced no primary copy of the note, so I treat them as a single secondary source; BofA's $85B and Citi's stale $77B [27] bracket them. I also note UBS's +40% revenue is bullish for EPS, not only for capex, and I reflect it in the bull case. Fair value rises from $397 to ~$418, still ~9% below spot. Skeptic findings are unchanged: no accounting, credit, insider or litigation red flags [9,10,12,13]. The bear case remains peak margins, AI concentration, rising capital intensity, rates, and the Taiwan/tariff tails [5,6,11]. Valuation-minded downgrades exist (GF Value $363 [28]; Hold/Buy downgrades [29]), but consensus is Strong Buy at ~$552 [29]. My 12-month median rises from $455 to $462: NTM EPS ~$23.9 at ~19-19.5x, with momentum and 9/0 revisions offsetting de-rating. The ladder is a 96% lognormal (median $462, sigma 0.36, trimmed from 0.38 because high rates argue for a thinner right tail) plus a 4% crash state (median $160, sigma 0.45) for a cross-strait shock. Polymarket's 13% [6] is a single market resolving after the horizon, so I keep that weight below it, as the supervisor also judged. Scenario mean is ~$466; lognormal-mixture mean is ~$480 with median ~$454. Research limits: Seeking Alpha and Benzinga were 403 in round 1, and the UBS note itself was not reachable.
